On Friday, Nvidia stock fell fourteen percent in a single day.
It was the seventh drop in a row.
And it came just days after the man who built the company walked away.
Jensen Huang started Nvidia in nineteen ninety-three, in a booth at a Denny's restaurant.
For thirty-three years, he was Nvidia.
He became famous for his black leather jacket, and for the chips behind the AI boom.
On November twelfth, he stepped down.
The strange part is that business has never been better.
On November seventeenth, Nvidia reported one hundred fifteen point eight billion dollars in revenue for a single quarter.
That is more than double a year ago.
Big tech companies keep buying its chips for their AI data centers.
Then Reuters reported that the SEC is looking at possible accounting problems at Nvidia.
So is this the end of the AI boom, or a chance to buy?
